evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires both snapshots to have nonempty, different manager PIDs and invocation IDs. It does not require the snapshots to come from the same boot. If the guest reboots between the restart command and the second inspect, the post-reboot manager has a different PID and invocation ID, so the predicate passes even though the observations span a guest reboot rather than proving an isolated manager restart. The smallest compatible fix is to also require nonempty equal `boot_id` values on the two manager snapshots while retaining the PID and invocation-ID inequality checks.
